optionReasons.saa-med-076:option:0: Sharing partitions data and replication copy data — are not cache POPULATION strategies.
optionReasons.saa-med-076:option:2: Cache warming is preload and cache busting is invalidate versions — wrong names for the described.
optionReasons.saa-med-076:option:3: The names are INVERTIDOS: load in miss is lazy loading; record each writing is write-through.

finalJustifications: Because (1) is lazy loading — population on demand, saves memory but can serve data out of date — and (2) is write-through — cache always fresh at double writing cost and possibly never read items.
Because lazy loading ensures that the cache never gets outdated: each miss revalidates the data against the bank before serving the answer to the end user.
Because write-through eliminates the need for TTL in the cache — with the writings always synchronized, the keys never need to expire or be invalidated.
Because the two strategies cannot be used together: the Redis engine requires you to choose a single cache population mode per cluster provided.

optionReasons.saa-med-085:option:0: Both models apply to the use per second of the EC2 — the form of PAGAMENTO is not the central difference.
optionReasons.saa-med-085:option:2: There is no discount on 100% — the ceilings are around 72-75%.
optionReasons.saa-med-085:option:3: Savings Plans cover EC2/Fargate/Lambda — no S3; and RIs also exist for RDS, ElestiCache etc..

finalJustifications: Because Savings Plan commits one VALOR (US$/h per 1-3 years) applied flexibly, and the IR commits a specific CONFIGURATION (type/region) — financial flexibility vs capacity rigidity.
Because Savings Plan is prepaid with credits consumed throughout the contract, and the IR is postpaid with discount applied directly on the monthly account bill.
Because the IR gives a bigger discount than any other Savings Plan in all scenarios — the flexibility of the plan is charged as an award on the final rate.
Because Savings Plan expires when the expenditure is below the amount committed, while the IR remains valid until the end of the signed use contract.

optionReasons.saa-med-086:option:0: Bare metal x86 larger is MAIS — no profit of price-performance.
optionReasons.saa-med-086:option:2: GPUs serve ML/graphics — extra cost without benefit for general workloads.
optionReasons.saa-med-086:option:3: Less larger instances do not change the price per performance unit — the same architecture, the same relative cost.

finalJustifications: Because Graviton (ARM, proposed by the AWS) delivery up to ~40% best price-performance, and portable workloads (JVM, Python, multi-arch containers) migrate without rewriting.
Because Graviton runs x86 code natively without recompilation, translating the instructions into hardware without performance cost.
Because Graviton instances are free in the first quarter of use, the incentive of AWS to the adoption of architecture ARM.
Because Graviton folds the memory of each instance at the same price, and it's the RAM extra that generates the perceived economy in the invoice.

optionReasons.saa-med-090:option:0: Export and truncate the table QUEBRARIA the application — is not cost management.
optionReasons.saa-med-090:option:1: GSIs ADICIONAM cost (own capacity) — do not divide anything.
optionReasons.saa-med-090:option:2: On-demand is NOT always cheaper: the price per request is higher; it compensates in unpredictable traffic, not in stable cargo.

finalJustifications: Because with stable and predictable traffic, provided capacity (with auto scaling On-demand unit price) delivers the same throughput at a much lower cost than on-demand unit price.
Because the provided mode eliminates the storage charge from the table, leaving only the cost of the contracted throughput per hour.
Because auto scaling of the provided zero capacity in idle periods, charging only the seconds of real traffic measured.
Because the provided mode gives retroactive discount on past use on-demand, compensating for late migration of the stable table.

optionReasons.saa-med-092:option:0: The GuardDuty detects security threats — no expenditure anomalies.
optionReasons.saa-med-092:option:1: Manual invoice review is just the slow process that fails today.
optionReasons.saa-med-092:option:3: The Budgets requires LIMIAR fixed defined by you — does not learn patterns or catch anomalies under the ceiling.

finalJustifications: Because Cost Anomaly Detection learns the pattern of spending per service/account/tag with ML and alerts deviations in days — without maintaining manual thresholds per service.
Because the Cost Anomaly Detection blocks the service that doubled the cost, containing the expense until the approval of the financial team.
Because Cost Anomaly Detection renegotiates tariffs with AWS when detecting anomaly, reversing the increase in the billing.
Because Cost Anomaly Detection works only with Savings Plans assets — it is the commitment that feeds the ML model.

optionReasons.saa-med-095:option:0: Third parties have prices MUITO different — Expedited is the most expensive per GB.
optionReasons.saa-med-095:option:1: Duplicate the file in EBS would multiply the cost of permanent storage — the opposite of the objective.
optionReasons.saa-med-095:option:2: Returning everything to the Standard permanently pays dearly the entire year for rarely used data.

finalJustifications: Because planned audits weeks in advance fit Bulk deadline (5-12(h) — the cheapest tier per GB, ideal for large volumes.
Because Bulk delivers data in minutes like Expedited, with the difference of being free for large volumes.
Because Bulk restores the files directly to EBS of audit instances, jumping the staging stage in the S3.
Because Bulk is the only ter that preserves the metadata of objects, requirement of conformity audits.

optionReasons.saa-med-099:option:0: Renaming accounts does not create a cost dimension in the reports — and does not cover rules of write-off.
optionReasons.saa-med-099:option:2: Manual spreadsheets are slow, error-prone and out of the tools of AWS.
optionReasons.saa-med-099:option:3: Separate organisations fragment entire governance — disproportionate to a RELATORIO problem.

finalJustifications: Because Cost Categories defines rules that map accounts, tags and services in business categories (with shared cost ratio) — visible in Cost Explorer, Budgets and CUR.
Because Cost Categories automatically creates tags in all account resources, standardizing the business dimensions at source.
Because the Cost Categories moves resources between accounts according to the rule of rate, consolidating each unit into its own billing account.
Because Cost Categories requires a dedicated billing account per business unit, where the default rules are applied monthly.

optionReasons.saa-med-100:option:1: Drift Detection compares stack to template — nothing to do with economy.
optionReasons.saa-med-100:option:2: ServiceLens application observability — does not recommend economy.
optionReasons.saa-med-100:option:3: The Resource Explorer BUSCA Account resources — does not prioritize cost opportunities.

finalJustifications: Because Cost Optimization Hub adds and prioritizes recommendations from various sources (Compute Optimizer, Trusted Advisor, Savings Plans) with economy and deduction estimation — the single FinOps panel.
Because Cost Optimization Hub automatically applies recommendations in the morning, performing right-sizing and removing idle features without manual approval.
Because Cost Optimization Hub is the mandatory prerequisite to purchase Savings Plans — the commitment recommendations are only valid within the official panel.
Because Cost Optimization Hub collects 1% of the economy generated as a success rate, the standard remuneration model of FinOps services managed from AWS.
